title: RanSOM: Second-Order Momentum with Randomized Scaling for Constrained and Unconstrained Optimization
abstract: arXiv:2602.06824v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Second-order momentum corrects the lag of momentum behind the current gradient with a Hessian-vector product (HVP), but existing corrections need either a Lipschitz Hessian or extra forward and backward passes at an auxiliary point. We show that randomizing the step length removes this trade-off: if the step is exponentially distributed with mean $\eta$, a Stein-type identity makes $\eta$ times one HVP at the new iterate an estimate of the gradient change that is unbiased in expectation over the step, and this HVP shares its forward pass with the next gradient. The resulting method, RanSOM-E, works with normalized, sign, and Muon-type steps, and a Beta-distributed variant, RanSOM-B, keeps Frank-Wolfe iterates feasible. For objectives with Lipschitz gradient and heavy-tailed gradient and Hessian noise with tail indices $p, q \in (1,2]$, RanSOM-E attains the optimal oracle-complexity exponents for every pair $(p,q)$, including $p

translated_title: RanSOM：用于约束与无约束优化的随机化缩放二阶动量方法
translated_abstract: arXiv:2602.06824v3 公告类型： replace-cross 摘要：二阶动量通过Hessian-向量积（HVP）来修正动量落后于当前梯度的滞后问题，但现有的修正方法要么需要Hessian满足Lipschitz条件，要么需要在辅助点进行额外的前向和反向传播。我们证明，将步长随机化可以消除这一权衡：如果步长服从均值为η的指数分布，一个Stein型恒等式使得新迭代点处的一次HVP乘以η成为梯度变化的无偏估计（对该随机步长的期望而言），并且该HVP的前向传播可以与下一次梯度计算共享。由此得到的方法RanSOM-E适用于归一化步长、符号步长和Muon型步长；而Beta分布变体RanSOM-B则能保持Frank-Wolfe迭代的可行性。对于梯度Lipschitz连续且梯度噪声和Hessian噪声均为重尾分布（尾指数p, q ∈ (1,2]）的目标函数，RanSOM-E对每一对都达到了最优的预言机复杂度指数，包括p...（原文在此截断）
tldr: 该论文提出RanSOM方法，通过将优化步长随机化（指数或Beta分布），利用Stein型恒等式使新迭代点处单次Hessian-向量积（且其前向传播可与下一次梯度计算共享）成为梯度变化的无偏估计，从而在无需Lipschitz Hessian或额外前向反向传播的情况下，对约束（Frank-Wolfe）和无约束优化均达到最优的oracle复杂度。
en_tdlr: RanSOM randomizes the optimization step length so that, via a Stein-type identity, a single Hessian-vector product at the new iterate—sharing its forward pass with the next gradient—becomes an unbiased estimate of the gradient change, achieving optimal oracle-complexity for both unconstrained and Frank-Wolfe constrained optimization without requiring a Lipschitz Hessian or extra forward/backward passes.
